Nyirgyulaj Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírgyulaj, Hungary

Not demolished. Jews first settled in Nyírgyulaj around 1770; population grew from 17 in 1840 to 139 by 1920, before declining sharply to 43 by 1944. The community joined the Orthodox stream after 1869's Schism but remained too small for independence, falling under Nyírbátor's larger jurisdiction while still maintaining its own synagogue, cheder, and burial society. By 1941 young men were conscripted for forced labor, effectively ending local religious life even before the 1944 deportation via the Nyíregyháza Ghetto to Auschwitz; only 4 Jews remained in the village by 1949. This cemetery's oldest tombstone dates to 1838, its newest to 1940.
